The defaults work for most vaults. This page explains the three choices
behind them, which embedding model turns text into vectors, which
language model answers, and which shelf a document lives on, so you can
tell when one of them no longer fits.

``` python
from tempfile import mkdtemp
from vishalakshi import Vault
from functools import partial
from vishalakshi.ask import CHAT_CACHE, CachedChat, use_chat
```

``` python
v = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'vault.db')
v.note('federate fuses the legs by rank because they share no vector space: the vault embeds '
       'prose, kosha embeds identifiers, ripgrep embeds nothing.', tags=['retrieval'])
v.add('# Late chunking\n\n## Method\n\nEmbed the whole document, then pool per chunk, so a chunk '
      'keeps the context around it.\n\n## Results\n\nEvaluated on BEIR.', 'Late chunking', kind='note')
with use_chat(partial(CachedChat, path=CHAT_CACHE)): v.connect()   # replays a recorded extraction; plain `v.connect()` asks the model
v.stats()
```

## What retrieval actually returns

`v.context(q)` is the retrieval underneath `ask`. It returns whole
sections, each with its breadcrumb and a `node_id` that `read` opens
again. The cell below prints each section’s length and breadcrumb. The
code hits at the end come from kosha and ripgrep, because this
repository is indexed.

``` python
c = v.context('why are rankings fused instead of distances?', sections=4, related=4)
for s in c.results: print(f'{len(s.text):5}  {s.breadcrumb}')
```

      141  federate fuses the legs by rank because they share no vector space: the vault em
       86  Late chunking › Method
       18  Late chunking › Results
      234  repo › /Users/71293/code/personal/orgs/vishalakshi/vishalakshi/code.py:57
      154  grep › index.ipynb:161
      600  repo › /Users/71293/code/personal/orgs/vishalakshi/vishalakshi/extract.py:179
       89  grep › 07_concepts.ipynb:101

``` python
for s in c.related: print(f'{s.via:6}  {s.breadcrumb}')
```

`results` are the sections that answer the question. `related` are the
sections nearest to them in vector space, useful as leads before you
know what to search for; they do not change the ranking of `results`.

``` python
c.encoder
```

    'minishlab/potion-multilingual-128M (256d, float16, model2vec)'

`c.encoder` always says which embedding model produced the vectors. With
`offline=True` the vault hashes character sequences instead of using a
model; `evals/encoder.py` measures what that costs against the default.

## Models and backends

A model is named by an id, and
[Rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi) works out which backend
runs it: LiteRT, MLX, llama.cpp or Ollama on this machine, or a hosted
API, which needs its API key. LiteRT is the default local path. The
backends and their options belong to Rishi and change with it, so this
page shows only what the vault passes through: `model=` and `chat_kw=`.

``` python
import rishi.core
from urai import Chat, infer_runtime
from vishalakshi.ask import dflt_model

# Rishi names and registers the backends. Urai resolves their model ids.
gemma4_e2b = 'litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm'
dflt_model, gemma4_e2b     # $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL if set, else the small local default
```

``` python
{m: infer_runtime(m) for m in (gemma4_e2b, 'mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit', 'my-local.gguf',
                               'gpt-5.6-luna', 'gemma-3-4b-it-int4')}
```

``` python
v.ask('why are rankings fused?', model=gemma4_e2b)             # an id: rishi knows what runs it
v.ask('why are rankings fused?', model='llama/my-local.gguf')  # a prefix when the id cannot say
v.ask('why are rankings fused?', model='mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit',
      chat_kw=dict(temp=0, think=True))          # the rest of rishi's constructor
```

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_fail
# `model=` plus `chat_kw=` is the model API. Urai reports an id that names no registered backend.
test_fail(lambda: Chat('gemma-3-4b-it-int4'), contains='backend')
```

A reasoning model writes its reasoning in a `<think>` block before the
answer. That block goes to `r.thinking`, not `r.answer`, because it
often mentions sections the model then sets aside, and citations are
read from the answer alone.

Retrieval never needs the network. Only answering with a hosted model
does.

## Encoders

An encoder, or embedding model, turns text into vectors so that texts
with similar meanings land near each other. The default is a static
multilingual model producing 256 numbers per text, stored as 16-bit
floats. `offline=True` hashes character sequences instead, which needs
no download but matches spelling rather than meaning. A shelf records
the encoder that wrote it.

``` python
Vault(':memory:', offline=True).enc.note      # never attempt a download; also the CI default
```

    'char-n-gram hashing (256d): lexical only; pass encoder= or restore network access for real semantics'

``` python
Vault(encoder='minishlab/potion-science-32M')   # pick a different one
```

    Vault('/Users/71293/.vishalakshi/vault.db': 0 docs, 0 chunks, 0 entities, encoder=model2vec)

16-bit floats are litesearch’s default width. One vector index holds one
encoder’s vectors, so documents embedded by different encoders need
different shelves.

`ENCODERS` holds three aliases, each a plain model id: `multilingual`,
the default; `code`, the model kosha uses for identifiers; and `gemma`,
the slowest and most faithful. Any other model2vec id works by name too.

``` python
from vishalakshi.core import ENCODERS

ENCODERS
```

A static model is a lookup table from words to vectors, so it embeds a
document in milliseconds without a GPU. litesearch measured weighted MRR
between 0.018 and 0.046 across four encoders, which is why the static
default is the chosen trade-off (`evals/encoder.py`). `gemma` is an ONNX
model, and choosing it is what loads onnxruntime.

``` python
# `encoder=` also takes any object with an `.encode`, which is what a shelf gets when you build one
import numpy as np
from vishalakshi.core import mk_encoder

class Eight:
    def encode(self, xs, **kw): return np.zeros((len(xs), 8), dtype=np.float16)

e = mk_encoder(Eight())
e.dims, e.method, e.name
```

One vector index is one vector space, so different encoders need
different shelves. `SHELVES` names the shelves the vault uses itself,
and `KIND_SHELF` says which kinds acquisition sends to their own shelf.

``` python
from vishalakshi.core import SHELVES, KIND_SHELF

SHELVES, KIND_SHELF
```

``` python
papers = v.shelf('papers')        # reuses the live encoder unless a registry entry exists
papers.add('# Late chunking\n\nWe evaluate contextual chunk embeddings on BEIR.', 'a paper')

[(s['store'], s['encoder'], s['docs']) for s in v.shelves()]
```

`KIND_SHELF` routes documents as they arrive. `reshelf` moves a document
later, once its doctype is known, and `elsewhere` searches the other
shelves.

``` python
v.route('arxiv').name, v.route('web').name
```

    ('papers', 'store')

A PDF may be an invoice or a paper, and its kind cannot tell which.
`categorize` decides after the document is filed, and `reshelf` moves it
to the shelf its doctype belongs on.

``` python
v.add('# Attention is all you need\n\n## Abstract\n\nWe propose the Transformer.\n\n'
      '## Introduction\n\nRelated work [1] et al.\n\n## References\n\ndoi:10.1/x',
      'attention', source='/inbox/attention.pdf')

r = v.reshelf('/inbox/attention.pdf', llm='never')
r.doctype, r.was, r.store, r.moved
```

    ('paper', 'store', 'papers', True)

``` python
v.doc('/inbox/attention.pdf'), v.shelf('papers').doc('/inbox/attention.pdf')['title']
```

    (None, 'attention')

Moving a document adds it to the new shelf from scratch, so its vectors
are made again by that shelf’s encoder, and the copy on the old shelf is
deleted. Its meta goes with it, with the doctype and the shelf it came
from. Marks are keyed to a document on its shelf, so they do not move
with it.

`federate` treats each shelf as one more search to merge by rank, beside
kosha and ripgrep. `elsewhere` adds a couple of sections from the
neighbouring shelves to `context` and `ask`.

``` python
v.federate('contextual chunk embeddings', repo=False, grep=False).legs
```

    {'prose': 3, 'shelf:papers': 4}

Each row from `elsewhere` names the shelf it came from in `store`. Pass
that to `read(node_id, store=...)` when the section is not on the
current shelf.

``` python
e = v.elsewhere('contextual chunk embeddings')
L(e).map(lambda r: (r.store, r.breadcrumb))
```

    [('papers', 'papers › a paper'),
     ('papers', 'papers › attention › Attention is all you need › Abstract')]

``` python
v.read(e[0].node_id, store=e[0].store)['text'][:80]
```

    '# Late chunking\n\nWe evaluate contextual chunk embeddings on BEIR.'

A shelf records the encoder that wrote it and reopens with the same one.
Opening it with a different encoder raises an error rather than mixing
two vector spaces. To change a shelf’s encoder on purpose, drop the
shelf and add its documents again.
